title: What If One Second Felt Like a Year? Part 2

shots.scene: wide rainy dusk street, traffic, slow push
the bus swings round the corner

shots.line: A girl on a bicycle, front wheel already over the curb.
shots.scene: Nova on her bike, front wheel over the curb, bus closing in
FREEZE: street stops, blue tint, rain hangs

shots.line: Raindrops hang in the air like glass beads.
shots.scene: insert: raindrops hanging like glass beads

shots.line: The bus driver’s mouth is open mid-shout.
shots.scene: insert: bus front, driver frozen mid-shout
Leo tiny on the frozen clock face, 1 SECOND = 1 YEAR

shots.line: But this time, a voice speaks inside your head.
shots.scene: gold ripples reach Leo's head from far away
whispered gold text: DON'T BREATHE OUT
frozen Nova close-up, eyes on the bus
frozen wide: bus inches from her front wheel
black: I DON'T MAKE IT fades

shots.line: Two weeks earlier, everything was finally calm.
shots.scene: calm bedroom morning, label TWO WEEKS EARLIER

shots.line: Hold your breath, and one second becomes a whole year.

shots.scene: insert: frozen hand with a lock

shots.line: Last time, that year helped you save your grandpa’s life.

shots.scene: Grandpa dances slower, rubs his back
Leo at the window at night

shots.line: It used to wait for you. Now it doesn’t.

shots.scene: car honks, Leo freezes on the sidewalk

shots.line: But inside, you’ve now lived fifty-two years.
So what happens when one second feels like a year... and you’re not the only one who knows?
Then, in the middle of a frozen year, you hear something new.
shots.scene: frozen year void, Leo alone, a flicker far away
Leo frozen in a shop, eyes strain
Nova frozen in her room, tint

shots.line: But somehow, you can think to each other.
shots.scene: two figures, thoughtLink between their heads
map: two houses, three streets apart

shots.line: And she’s had the same power...
How many years have you lived in here?
shots.scene: Leo thinks the question across the link

shots.line: You thought fifty was a lot.
Plus: for the first time, the year isn’t silent.

shots.scene: bubbles of topics fly between them

shots.line: Why cats knock things off tables.
shots.scene: cat pushes a cup off a table

shots.line: You play chess with no board, just in your heads.
Minus: she knows where this is going.
Now one second feels like two.
In the real world, you finally meet on a park bench.
shots.scene: park bench, Leo and Nova sit

shots.line: But where it gets really strange...
shots.scene: tilt up from the bench to the night sky

shots.line: In her years, Nova stares upward, so she counts stars.
shots.scene: Nova eyes up, stars tick off

shots.line: The light from some of those stars left them hundreds of years ago, she tells you.
shots.scene: star -> earth light ray, HUNDREDS OF YEARS

shots.line: We’re both looking at the past.
shots.scene: both on the bench under the stars, silhouette

shots.line: Four thousand, one hundred and twelve.
Every time she breathes out, the real world feels too fast.
shots.scene: busy street rushes too fast around Nova
Nova in the void, years counter rising

shots.line: People returning from long isolation often struggle to adjust, even to ordinary noise and crowds.
shots.scene: research card: long isolation -> noise and crowds overwhelming

shots.line: Sometimes I think I should just...

shots.scene: word STAY fades in the dark

shots.line: What if one day... you can’t breathe out?
shots.scene: breath icon locked: CAN'T BREATHE OUT?

shots.line: Now someone else is living it.
shots.scene: Nova drifting deeper into the void

shots.line: And she’s starting to like it.
So you bring her to Sunday dinner.
shots.scene: kitchen wide: Leo brings Nova, Grandpa waves

shots.line: About a hundred beats a minute.
It kept me alive, young lady.
Then he gives her the line.

shots.scene: words continue: IF YOU USE IT

shots.line: You notice one thing about her that night.
Before anything scary, Nova counts down.

shots.scene: Nova at a desk with a test
Nova and a spoon of soup
Leo walks with his hood up

shots.line: Across the street, Nova waits on her bike.
shots.scene: Nova waits on her bike across the street

shots.line: And a bus swings round the corner.
shots.scene: the bus swings round the corner
gold link from Nova's frozen head
frozen wide: bus at her wheel

shots.line: The bus is about ten meters from her front wheel.
At fifty kilometers per hour, it covers that in under a second.
And it needs more than twenty meters to stop.
shots.scene: stopping distance 20+ m past the bike
frozen: three footprints from Leo to Nova

shots.line: Your body still needs about a quarter of a second just to start moving.

shots.scene: Leo total vs bus arrival, neck and neck

shots.line: And part of you wants it.

shots.scene: Leo's grey empty years fade away
balance: STAY FOREVER vs STEP OUT NOW

shots.line: Then you hear Grandpa’s beat in your head.

shots.scene: insert: hand grabs the backpack strap
the bus roars past, motion blur

shots.line: close enough to lift her hair.
Her front wheel stops right on the curb.
shots.scene: insert: front wheel on the curb
both laughing wide in the rain

shots.line: On Sunday, Nova comes to dinner again.
And this time, she doesn’t count down.
For the first time in two hundred years...
That night, the power takes you again.
And a voice speaks inside the year.
There are two of you now.
shots.scene: stranger, two gold lights reflected in his glasses

shots.line: I’ve been waiting a very long time.
So what would you do with a year inside one second?
shots.scene: Leo looks up at the clock

shots.line: Tell us who you’d share it with in the comments. And if you held your breath when Nova counted down... hit like, and subscribe for Part Three.
